messages:
sara: started canary for mariner-6b-ptq-4bit at 09:12 PT, seeing weird sampling oscillation + 95th percentile latency spikes. filing here so eng-ml can triage. :warning:

ajay: can you paste an example prompt/response where sampling oscillation shows up?

sara: short repro below — hitting repeated token jitter (different runs produce wildly different continuations). temp=0.8, top_p=0.92, seed not fixed. example prompt:
```
Prompt: 
Write a short product description for an eco-friendly notebook.
```
Responses vary: some finish fine, others start looping on adjectives then cut off. also noticed p95 latency goes from ~120ms to ~420ms for the same seq len.

mei: timeline? is this immediately after onboard/quant?

sara: post-canary rollout (we enabled mariner-6b-ptq-4bit as canary on 3% traffic about 09:10). prior to rollout fp16 variant was stable.

lucas: ops-bot traces?

ops-bot: deploy notice: canary mariner-6b-ptq-4bit v2026-03-20-0910 deployed to cluster-west-1.

ajay: possible culprits: 1) sampling randomness amplified by aggressive quantization, 2) KV cache eviction/rewind glitches causing repeated prefixes, 3) batching/compaction interaction with fused kernels under 4-bit. need logs.

mei: capture model logs and per-token timing for the slow requests. also check if kernel fallback happened (e.g., to slower kernel path).

lucas: pulled a slow trace — attached snippet:
```
[trace id: 0x9f2b]
step 1: allocate kv cache ok
step 2: fused_attn dispatch -> fallback to generic_attn (reason: unsupported block size)
step 3: generate tokens 1-12: mean 10ms/token
step 4: generate tokens 13-50: mean 55ms/token (spike)
```

ajay: fallback to generic_attn would explain latency. why would fused_attn fallback only for some requests? maybe seq length threshold or alignment bug for particular tokenization.

mei: do we have quantization parity tests vs fp16 on the same inputs? if sampling distribution diverges post-quant, that explains oscillation. run a 50-seed batch with fixed seeds for fp16 vs ptq and compare logits and top-k choices.

sara: starting parity run now; will upload diffs to the canary folder.

lucas: quick mitigation: revert canary routing to fp16 for mariner-6b until we diagnose. can we do a rollback?

ops-bot: rollback command queued by lucas: `/rollout set-route mariner-6b canary=0.0 fp16=1.0` — confirm with :thumbsup:.

ajay: agreed revert to fp16 for 0.5 hours while we triage. also flag for QA to run sampling stability harness.

mei: triage checklist I'm going to run:
- reproduce locally with same tokenizer and prompt using both backends (fp16 vs 4bit PTQ)
- compare logits/topk for first 64 tokens across 50 seeds
- check kernel selection traces for each request, and kernel selection rules in runtime
- inspect KV cache alignment for batch sizes 1..8 and seq lens 16..256
- run unit that forces fused_attn path vs forces generic_attn to compare outputs

ajay: add to checklist: check temperature / sampling impl differences (e.g., our fused sampler had a minor transform). also examine whether prefix caching is returning stale prefixes when quantized keys collide numerically.

sara: assigned owners: mei -> reproduce + parity diffs, ajay -> runtime/kernel trace + sampler impl review, lucas -> rollback + canary routing + perf dashboards, sara -> postmortem + customer comms if needed.

lucas: perf dashboards show p95 spike correlates with requests routed to node-group g-west-4. canary was pinned to that group. moving canary off group now.

ops-bot: route update applied: mariner-6b-ptq-4bit canary traffic set to 0.0.

mei: quick update after 20m: parity run shows the PTQ logits diverge for ~12% of tokens beyond top10; in many cases the top candidate differs which leads to different sampling cascades. fusion fallback correlates with requests that have token ids % 64 in range 0..7 (suspicious alignment).

ajay: hypothesis: PTQ kernel expects packed tensors with 64-bit alignment; certain tokenizer outputs cause misaligned attention blocks causing runtime to fallback. fallback route hits an unoptimized path which also seems to sample differently (maybe due to float casting).

mei: next step: create focused test that pads tokens to force alignment and see if fused_attn gets used consistently and if sampling matches fp16.

sara: priority? this is high for canary but low customer impact (canary only). recommend we keep ptq disabled in prod until fix.

ajay: estimate 1-2d to root cause and small runtime patch to kernel selection. if sampler bug found, patch might be quicker.

lucas: logging action items in the canary incident ticket. tagging infra/cuda and runtime teams for kernel review. @infra-devs please peek.

ops-bot: incident ticket created: INC-2026-0419-67 (canary mariner-6b ptq sampling oscillation).

sara: thanks — I'll update when parity diffs uploaded. for now we've reverted traffic and isolated the canary nodes. :white_check_mark:

mei: uploaded parity diffs to s3://redwood-canary/mariner6b/parity/3425012345/diffs.tar.gz

ajay: once we have diffs, I'll run a delta-debug to see whether it's quant noise or kernel path. will update later today.

lucas: thumbs up. if anyone sees customer-visible regressions, ping on #incidents and we'll promote remediation.
